I really liked the way that Fallout: New Vegas made some dialogue options dependent on character build choices. On the recommendation of a friend I tried Mass Effect 2, which was (according to him) the best entry in the Mass Effect series. Its dialogue is interesting enough for one playthrough, and some dialogue choices only become available if you have enough "paragon" or "renegade" points. For the most part, though, I am only breezing through as a visual tourist. I like the visuals, but not enough to play through Mass Effect 2 as many times as I played through Fallout: New Vegas.

However the shortcomings of Mass Effect 2 make me wonder whether I would be happier with Divinity: Original Sin 2 or Tides of Numenera. I have gotten spoiled with modern graphical eye candy. Even though old-fashioned isometric RPGs often have good writing and relatively few bugs, I find them so visually ugly that I have trouble picking them up again. Thus I am playing through Mass Effect 2 with its glorious neon vector graphics and run-and-gun sprinting instead of going back to Tides of Numenera with its clunky sprites and slow navigation. But if I really want dialogue that depends on character build and choices, I probably should focus on games that are known for their deep writing - even if that means laboriously clicking through isometric landscapes.

I guess that the writing budget suffers when the developers feel a need to throw glorious visuals at the player. That would explain why the developers of Disco Elysium chose to go with an ugly isometric engine: they wanted their writing to be the star of the show. And maybe if that game had performed with fewer glitches, I would have finished it. So to sum up, CRPGs will save the world. Thanks for coming to my TED talk. blog post.
Dialogue in Mass Effect 2 versus dialogue in Fallout: New Vegas (and the contrast to Tides of Numenera or Divinity: Original Sin 2)

Tides of numenera was kind of a let down for me. Lots of great dialogue, but at the end I found myself thinking “so that’s it...huh.” Just not a satisfying game for me. No desire to start another play through ever since and I bought it at release.

I think all the Mass Effect titles can stand on their own, and the ME series is kind of a unique bird in that the pressure from EA was to keep reaching a broader and broader audience with each title.

This results in ME1 starting as a slow paced 'hard' RPG with some very technical gunplay based on equipment, but really it's just a vehicle to surround the dialogue and role-play.

Then ME2 focuses more on the gunplay and reduces dialogue somewhat, and ME3 does this even further.

Altogether I take them as three nice points along the action-RPG scale, each with different ratios of action to RPG.

The first instinct people have when they hear about the 'pure' version of ME1 and the influence of EA is to claim that it was the best and all the others fell in quality, but this wasn't really the case until the abortion that is Andromeda - which nobody shall speak of, for reasons we all know.

If you liked ME2 as a visual playthrough, I would recommend you check out ME3 as it looks gorgeous and the gameplay is very smooth. There is even a "Cinematic Mode" which reduces all dialogue to preset responses and essentially turns the game into a shooter.

I would only encourage you to dip into ME1 if you want a slower pace than ME2 and more thoughtful combat. The character development is worth it, and the gunplay is still fun, but it's quite a different beast than ME2 or ME3.
